Ardha-nārīśvara
(‘Lord, who is half-woman’)
------------------------------------------
Śiva, also called ईश्वर, is the third deity of the Hindu Trinity. He is generally worshipped in the form of the लिङ्ग.
Etymologically both the words, शिव and लिङ्ग, mean ‘that into which the universe dissolves’. शिव is thus the ultimate source of all च्रेअतिओन्.
In the Hindu mythological works, the शक्ति or power by which God creates, sustains and dissolves the universe is pictured as a female deity, the consort of God. शिव’s consort is पार्वती.
Ardhanārīśvara is one of the several forms in which शिव manifested himself. The right half is that of शिव and the left, that of पार्वती. This iconographic concept signifies the identity of शिव and शक्ति, and as a corollary, that man and woman are mutually complementary. In a more general sense, it signifies the bipolar nature of the world.
Some scholars opine that the form might have been evolved to bring about a compromise between the cults of शिव and शक्ति.

ardha-kṛcchra
(‘half कृच्छ्र;)
------------------------------------------
Sin (pāpa) and its expiation (prāya-ścitta) is one of the topics discussed by the धर्मशास्त्रस्, often in great detail. Many of the expiatory rites have been given the general name ‘kṛcchra’ (‘that which cuts happiness or causes suffering). Out of the several kṛcchras, the ‘ardha-कृच्छ्र’ is an expiation for minor sins and causes only ’half‘ the suffering of a कृच्छ्र (ardha = half).
The repentant transgressor is expec-ted to subsist on ड़ोओद् obtained without asking for it, for the first three days and thereafter fast completely for three more days.
As per another rule, he should eat only once in a day for two days, subsist on ड़ोओद् got unasked for two more days and fast completely for the last two days of the six day discipline.
See also KṚCCHRA.

ardha-maṇḍapa
(‘half-open hall’)
------------------------------------------
The most important part of a Hindu temple is the गर्भगृह (sanctum sanctorum) wherein is housed the idol of the deity. In front of it and contiguous to it is the मुखमण्डप, also called शुकनासी and ardhamaṇḍapa. This is actually a passage, its proportion being relative to that of the गर्भगृह itself. Apart from being used as a passage it is also used to keep the articles of worship including ड़ोओद् offerings on special occasions. The word is sometimes spelt as ‘ardhamanṭapa’ also.
